page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 8.0 GB, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or integrated hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-threaded CPU capability, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2924.48 placing in the top quartile of tested instances. However, multi-core throughput reflects the modest physical core count, yielding 5863.06 in stress-ng multi-core and 3743.0 in Geekbench multi-core testing. Memory performance shows 44.87 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 28.8 GB/sec for write operations, though aggregate memory scores remain lower relative to broader instance classes. The system achieves 28.27 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 142.61 tokens per second on text generation with small language models.

With its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and absence of bundled local storage, c2d-highcpu-4 delivers a dense compute footprint for CPU-bound tasks requiring modest working memory. The instance is suited for lightweight batch computation, CI/CD build runners, dedicated API microservices, and front-end web proxy routing. Workloads requiring substantial memory footprint, high concurrent thread scalability, or local high-speed disk I/O should evaluate larger instance tiers or memory-optimized alternatives.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor features 32 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for AES, VAES, SHA, and AVX instructions. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence. In benchmark evaluations, c2d-highcpu-4 demonstrates strong single-core CPU execution, achieving 2924.48 in stress-ng single-core tests, while multi-core throughput and memory subsystem benchmarks reflect the compact two-core footprint. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 44.87 GB/sec with write speeds of 28.8 GB/sec. This configuration is best suited for compute-focused, single-thread-reliant workloads, lightweight build pipelines, API gateways, and web application serving with limited memory footprints.
